The case of the prosecution is that the petitioner had introduced one Mr. Ashutosh Patnaik to respondent No. 2/School with an understanding that Ashutosh Patnaik will arrange for students participation in international conference.

It is further the case of the prosecution that 17 students of respondent No. 2/School paid Rs.27.2 lakhs into the account of the company of Ashotosh Pattanayak who is running the business in United Kingdom.

5. The learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the said amount was transferred to the account of the company of Ashutosh Patnaik and no amount was directly paid to the present petitioner.

He submits that in fact the petitioner herself is a victim of the misleading assurances given by Ashutosh Patnaik and the petitioner has also made a complaint against him on 03.07.2022, which is Annexure A4 to the present petition.

He further submits that the complaint made by the petitioner is prior in point of time than the FIR registered at the instance of respondent No. 2.
6. Issue notice.
7.
Learned Additional Standing Counsel accepts notice.
He submits that the petitioner was in connivance with the aforesaid Ashutosh Patnaik and there is every possibility that the money has been passed on by said This is a digitally signed order.

8. Let a status report be filed before the next date.
9.

In the meanwhile, no coercive action be taken against the present petitioner till the next date of hearing, subject to her joining investigation and further subject to the condition that she shall not leave the country.

10. List on 12.01.2024.
